issue.title: task: sync Zendesk ticket lifecycle with age review clock
issue.body:
Two improvements to keep Zendesk and relay-manager age review clocks in sync:

1. **Create Zendesk ticket at case creation/restriction**, not just at parent contact submission. Agents should see the case in Zendesk from the start.

2. **Set the Age Review Deadline custom field** on the ticket using the `deadline_at` value from the relay-manager case. Keeps the Zendesk queue's deadline column populated and in sync with the authoritative relay-manager clock.

Relay-manager clock remains authoritative (auto-closes expired cases). Zendesk deadline field provides agent visibility in their existing workflow.

Future consideration: sync clock pause/resume to the Zendesk deadline field. Lower priority since agents see the parent reply in the ticket itself.

issue.title: Age review: Zendesk integration for parent contact workflow
issue.body:
## Context

PR #67 adds the age review clock — 15-day case management for under-16 reports. When a flagged user submits their parent's email via the mobile app, the email is saved to the case and the clock pauses. Currently, the moderator sees the email in the admin UI and handles outreach manually.

This issue adds Zendesk automation so parent contact is tracked as a ticket with proper threading, SLA, and reply detection.

## Scope

### Outbound: auto-create Zendesk ticket on parent email submission

When `POST /v1/minor-review-cases/{caseId}/parent-contact` saves the parent email:

- Create a Zendesk ticket addressed to the parent email
- Template body explains the situation, asks parent to reply to verify
- Tag the ticket `age-review` + include case ID in a custom field or internal note
- Use existing Zendesk API patterns from `worker/src/index.ts` (ticket creation, custom fields)
- Non-blocking: ticket creation failure should not fail the parent-contact endpoint (log + continue)

### Inbound: webhook on parent reply

- New endpoint: `POST /api/zendesk/age-review-reply` (sits alongside existing `/api/zendesk/` routes, uses Zendesk webhook auth)
- Zendesk trigger: when a ticket tagged `age-review` receives a new reply from the requester, fire webhook
- Handler matches ticket to case (by case ID in custom field or by requester email lookup)
- Updates case: log that parent contact was received, optionally transition state to `submitted_for_review`
- Moderator still makes the final clear/deny decision

### Zendesk-side configuration

- New trigger: "Age review — parent replied" (condition: tag `age-review`, requester replied)
- Webhook target pointing at `POST /api/zendesk/age-review-reply` on the worker
- Custom field or tag convention for linking ticket to case ID
- Email template for outbound parent notification

## Dependencies

- PR #67 (age review clock) must be merged first
- `ZENDESK_API_TOKEN` and `ZENDESK_EMAIL` env vars (already available on the worker for existing Zendesk integration)

## Not in scope

- Auto-closing cases based on Zendesk ticket resolution (moderator decision stays manual)
- Parent identity verification beyond "they replied to the email"
- Multi-language email templates (English only for MVP)

review.body: Re-reviewed at b226a02. The original blocking schema-safety issue is fixed, and the remaining closeout gap I called out is now covered by worker entrypoint tests for /api/zendesk/age-review-reply (valid signed request and invalid signature path). Validation on the updated branch is clean enough to merge: root test command passed, worker vitest passed (142/142), frontend tsc passed, and the existing unrelated worker tsc failures remain outside this PR.

Requesting changes before merge. The blocking issue is schema safety on existing D1 databases: this adds the new column to fresh schemas and ships a migration, but ensureSchema() still does not self-heal existing age_review_cases tables, so deploy ordering can break parent-contact writes and the inbound webhook lookup. I left inline comments on the specific spots. I also called out the webhook secret naming/docs mismatch and the unrelated ReportWatcher log-scope expansion so those are reviewed intentionally.

comment.body: This log expansion is unrelated to the age-review Zendesk change. I’m not objecting to full pubkey/event-id logging here on its own, but it’s scope creep in a PR that otherwise stays tightly focused. Please either split this into a separate change or call it out explicitly in the PR description so it gets conscious review.

comment.body: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS only fixes fresh DBs. Existing staging/prod tables created before 0008 will not pick up this new column unless the migration is applied in perfect lockstep. Please mirror the existing reporter_pubkey pattern here with a best-effort ALTER TABLE age_review_cases ADD COLUMN zendesk_ticket_id INTEGER inside ensureSchema() so the webhook lookup and ticket-link write self-heal on older databases too.

This creates an `open_reported` case from a single `NS-underageUser` pubkey report with no trusted-client or moderator-review gate. Combined with `handleGetModerationStatus()` returning `restrictedMinorReview` for every non-terminal case, one unsolicited report is enough to surface a restricted-state payload to mobile before a human looks at it. If mobile actually enforces on that status, this is a real abuse/regression risk; if it does not, that contract needs to be explicit and covered by tests before merge.

This endpoint still bypasses `VALID_TRANSITIONS`. A client can hit `POST /v1/minor-review-cases/:id/parent-contact` while the case is still `open_reported`, `under_moderator_review`, or `needs_follow_up`, and this raw SQL will jump it straight into `restricted_pending_parental_consent` / `restricted_pending_support_email` without ever passing through the server-side state-machine guard added above. Please route this through the same transition validation and add a regression test for the mobile path.

comment.body:
Pushed follow-up fix in commit 3919934 to close the remaining age-review workflow gap.

What changed:
- The Age Review detail panel now derives the Restrict Account target state from the age band instead of treating every non-age_16_plus_claimed case the same.
- under_13 now routes to restricted_pending_support_email, which matches the shared resolution model and avoids sending those cases into the user-response path that mobile rejects.
- Added a frontend regression test covering all three band mappings:
  - under_13 -> restricted_pending_support_email
  - age_13_15 -> restricted_pending_user_response
  - age_16_plus_claimed -> restricted_pending_support_email

Validation run on the updated PR head:
- npm run test
- npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit
- cd worker && npx vitest run

All passed. The existing repo warnings during frontend lint/build are unchanged and pre-existing.
Fixed — deep link now passes hex pubkey (`c.pubkey`) instead of npub.

Fixed — `handleParentContact` now validates the transition against `VALID_TRANSITIONS` before modifying the case. If the current state doesn't allow advancing to `restricted_pending_parental_consent` / `restricted_pending_support_email`, it returns 400. This means the endpoint only works from `restricted_pending_user_response` (for 13–15) as intended — calling it from `open_reported`, `under_moderator_review`, or `needs_follow_up` is now rejected. New test covers the `open_reported` rejection path.

Valid concern. Fixed — `handleGetModerationStatus` now only returns `restrictedMinorReview` for moderator-reviewed states (`under_moderator_review`, `restricted_pending_*`, `submitted_for_review`, `needs_follow_up`). Cases in `open_reported` return `active` to mobile, so a single unsolicited report can't restrict the user before a human confirms. New test verifies `open_reported` returns `active`.

The trusted-client gate on case creation is a separate question — right now any `NS-underageUser` report creates a case. That's acceptable with this fix since `open_reported` is now inert from mobile's perspective, but if we want to gate creation too (e.g., require trusted client tag like auto-hide does), that can be a follow-up.

review.body: Requesting changes before merge. Two blocking issues remain: the mobile parent-contact path still bypasses the shared age-review state machine, and the current report-to-restriction flow appears to let a single unsolicited underage report surface `restrictedMinorReview` before moderator review. I don't think this is safe to merge until both are resolved or the mobile contract is made explicit and tested.

comment.body:
Fixed — added a `VALID_TRANSITIONS` map in the shared module (`shared/age-review.ts`) and server-side enforcement in `handleUpdateAgeReviewCase`. Invalid transitions return 400 with a descriptive error (`Cannot transition from 'X' to 'Y'`). New test covers the rejection path.

The map encodes the reachable transitions from the UI and mobile endpoints. Terminal states have empty arrays (already blocked by the existing closed-case check above, but the map is explicit).

Fixed — added `useEffect` that resyncs `resolutionNote` from props when `c.id` or `c.resolution_note` changes. The second dep handles same-case server refreshes (e.g., after TanStack Query invalidation).

Fixed — added `last_alerted_at` column (migration 0007) and a 12-hour dedupe filter in the approaching-deadline query. The column is stamped only after a successful Slack delivery (`sendSlackAlert` now returns `boolean`), so a failed webhook doesn't burn the dedupe window. Two new tests cover both paths.

Expired-case alerts don't need dedupe since the case transitions to `denied_closed` on the same cron run.

review.body: Re-ran validation against commit 0104a9e1990a7ed6b4725d9be400459abda2422d. The earlier regressions called out in review are fixed: hls.js is split into a separate async chunk, the manual media toggle is preserved after report data loads, and the stale worker CORS assertions were removed. Validation run: npm test, npx vite build, and worker Vitest suite all passed locally.

Requesting changes before merge. The current implementation has a few correctness issues that can break moderator workflows or create avoidable operational noise:

1. The Age Review detail deep link passes an npub into the Users route, but the selected-user workflow expects a hex pubkey and uses it directly in status checks and moderation actions.
2. The resolution note textarea does not resync when switching between cases, so a note typed on one case can be submitted for another.
3. The admin update endpoint accepts arbitrary enum-to-enum state changes even though this feature is described as a state machine; transition rules need to be enforced server-side.
4. Deadline alerts have no dedupe, so approaching cases will page Slack on every cron run until expiry.

comment.body: This will send the same approaching-deadline Slack alert on every cron run until the case expires or changes state. Without a dedupe marker like `last_alerted_at` or a separate alert log, this will create repeated operational noise for the same case.

The PR description calls this a state machine, but the server currently accepts any enum value here with no transition validation. That makes the API the source of new tech debt: any admin client or script can move a case into impossible states, and the mobile contract depends on these states being coherent. Please enforce allowed transitions server-side.

This state is initialized from props once and never resynced when `caseData` changes. If a moderator types a note on case A and then selects case B, the textarea can still contain case A text and submit it for case B. This needs a prop-to-state sync or a different state ownership model so notes cannot bleed across cases.

This link is building `/users/${npub}`, but the selected-user flow in `UserManagement` treats the route param as a hex pubkey and uses it directly for status checks and ban/allow mutations. Following this link can therefore show the wrong status and send an npub into NIP-86 calls. Pass the hex pubkey in the route, or make the Users route normalize npub inputs before any comparisons or mutations.

review.body: Requesting changes before merge. I re-ran the relevant validation locally and found three issues that should be fixed before this lands: the committed PR state leaves the worker test suite broken after the CORS header revert, `hls.js` is being pulled into the main bundle for a rare fallback path, and the new `showByDefault` sync can override a moderator's manual toggle when reports finish loading.

comment.body: This fixes the initial flash/collapse race, but it also means any later `showByDefault` transition from `false` to `true` will overwrite a moderator's manual toggle. In `ReportDetail`, `showByDefault` now starts false while reports are loading and then flips to true when `hasHighPriorityReports === false`, so this effect will reopen media even if the user explicitly hid it. Please preserve explicit user intent here and only apply the async default without clobbering a manual toggle.

This eager import pulls `hls.js` into the main app bundle even though it is only used after native video playback fails. I built both revisions locally: `origin/main` produces a ~964 kB minified main chunk (~270 kB gzip), while this branch jumps to ~1491 kB (~433 kB gzip). That is a large regression for a rare fallback path. Please move this to a dynamic `import('hls.js')` inside the fallback branch so the cost is only paid when the fallback is actually needed.

This assertion became stale in the second commit. `fix: remove global CORS credentials` removed `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` from `buildCorsHeaders`, but these two expectations stayed behind, so `cd worker && npx vitest run` fails on the committed PR state. Please drop the leftover credential assertions here and in the matching preview-origin test below so the documented worker suite stays green.
